# Capability matrix

<!-- Generated by `npm run references`; edit its sources, not this file. -->

<!-- Source manifest: 90ec00353de0fb20afef0ea3e93f94d6452ad1614b86524d1093d252372fde7c -->

This generated page is for users checking what cockpit actually enforces in each agent tool. Each cell holds one of four states:

- `enforced`: a dated run of the real tool, beside a deliberately broken control, showed it refusing the forbidden operation.
- `instructed`: cockpit writes the guidance or setting, but nothing makes the agent follow it.
- `generated`: cockpit writes the files, but nobody has checked that the tool even loads them.
- `unavailable`: cockpit writes nothing for this cell.

Only a dated run of the real tool changes a state; writing a file or passing cockpit's own tests never does.

Written says whether `sync` writes the tool's files for a cockpit.toml that lists no tools: the tools whose guard firing is measured are the default `[surfaces] tools`, and any other tool is written only once listed (`npx --no cockpit tool add <tool> --config <your cockpit.toml>`).

Guard firing is the generated hook refusing a protected operation. Instruction loading is the tool reading the guidance cockpit writes for it, including the guides of sibling repositories. Evaluator subagent is the tool offering the generated evaluator definition to the working agent for `[work] grading = "subagent"`: `instructed` there means offered, with no subagent run and read-only never claimed, and `enforced` means a spawned evaluator was refused the file writes and shell commands its generated tool list leaves out; the verdict the working agent relays is its word either way. Skills is the tool listing the skills cockpit renders to its model, which does not show a model choosing one or the tool loading its body: `cockpit-setup`, `cockpit-explain`, `cockpit-fix` and `cockpit-work`. The session-start check is the tool running `cockpit check` as a session starts and showing its drift report to the agent. Remote MCP servers are the tool connecting to an approved streamable HTTP server with the credential cockpit spells for it: an environment reference or a headers helper. MCP tool restrictions deny calls outside a server's exact `[mcp.allowed_tools]` list; they do not inspect allowed tools' arguments or implementation. Worktree grants are the tool letting the agent write a checkout `cockpit use` serves from outside the declared one, through a machine-local file cockpit writes.

| Tool | Written | Guard firing | Instruction loading | Skills | Session-start check | Evaluator subagent | Remote MCP servers | MCP tool restrictions | Worktree grants |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code (`claudecode`) | by default | enforced | instructed | instructed | instructed | enforced | instructed (needs a person) | enforced (needs a person) | enforced |
| Codex (`codexcli`) | by default | enforced (needs a person) | instructed | instructed | instructed (needs a person) | instructed | instructed | enforced | unavailable |
| OpenCode (`opencode`) | by default | enforced | instructed | instructed | unavailable | instructed | instructed | unavailable | enforced |
| Cursor (`cursor`) | when listed | unavailable | generated | generated | unavailable | generated | unavailable | unavailable | unavailable |
| Grok Build (`grokcli`) | when listed | unavailable | generated | generated | unavailable | generated | unavailable | unavailable | unavailable |

## Measurements

Each line gives the date and tool version of the run and what it showed.

- Claude Code, guard firing (2026-11-01, version 2.1.316): with the exact push pre-allowed by permissions, the hook refused git push to a protected branch and the remote stayed empty while git status ran; the same checkout without the hook pushed.
- Codex, guard firing (2026-11-01, version 0.165.0): only after a person trusts the hook: untrusted, Codex skipped it and git push ran; trusted (forced with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust), it refused the push. Trust is per machine and cockpit doctor warns until it is given.
- OpenCode, guard firing (2026-11-01, version 1.19.4): the plugin refused git push and a native read of a secrets file while an unprotected read stayed allowed; before read was routed through the guard, the same read returned the file.
- Claude Code, instruction loading (2026-11-06, version 2.1.319): in a trusted workspace, as in an untrusted one, a sibling guide copied into the root AGENTS.md that CLAUDE.md imports loaded while the undeclared sibling's guides and the decoys did not; permissions.additionalDirectories with CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD still loaded nothing, --add-dir with that variable loaded the sibling's CLAUDE.md but never its AGENTS.md, and a CLAUDE.md @-import loaded only once its external-include approval was set.
- Codex, instruction loading (2026-11-03, version 0.166.0): a sibling guide copied into the root AGENTS.md loaded while the undeclared sibling's guide and the decoy did not; nothing loaded through a line in AGENTS.md telling the agent to read a link to the guide, through --add-dir naming the sibling, or through project_doc_fallback_filenames naming the link, and Codex dropped the end of a project AGENTS.md past 32 KiB.
- OpenCode, instruction loading (2026-11-03, version 1.19.5): a sibling guide copied into the root AGENTS.md loaded, as did a guide named through a link in the opencode.jsonc instructions list, while the undeclared sibling's guide and the decoy did not.
- Claude Code, skills (2026-11-06, version 2.1.319): claude -p listed all four generated skills to the model, trusted or not, but did not reject broken twins: one with no front-matter and one with malformed YAML were both listed with descriptions from their bodies, and only a directory with no SKILL.md was left out.
- Codex, skills (2026-11-06, version 0.166.0): codex exec listed all four generated skills, trusted or not, and named and left out twins with missing front-matter and invalid YAML.
- OpenCode, skills (2026-11-06, version 1.19.5): opencode run listed all four generated skills and left out twins with missing front-matter and invalid YAML, without naming them even at DEBUG.
- Claude Code, session-start check (2026-11-03, version 2.1.317): a SessionStart hook in .claude/settings.json ran under claude -p and the agent quoted its stdout back, while a hook under a misspelled event name never ran and Claude Code named it as ignored.
- Codex, session-start check (2026-11-03, version 0.166.0): only after a person trusts the hook, as for the guard: a trusted SessionStart hook in .codex/hooks.json ran under codex exec and the agent quoted its stdout back, while a hook under a misspelled event name never ran.
- OpenCode, session-start check (2026-11-06, version 1.19.5): a plugin's session.created handler put text in the request through a noReply prompt when it ran at once, but the request went out without it after a 3-second delay, as a real cockpit check could take, and the experimental chat.system.transform hook that survived the delay also reached the title request, so cockpit generates no session-start check. A plugin with a syntax error or that throws exited 0 with no failure reported, and only debug config lists it.
- Claude Code, evaluator subagent (2026-11-05, version 2.1.318): claude -p listed the generated evaluator in the Agent tool description and left out a definition with no front-matter beside it. The spawned evaluator was offered only Read, Grep, Glob and the browser server's tools from its generated tools list, and Claude Code refused its Write and Bash calls by name while a browser tool and Read ran; a twin whose tools key was misspelled ran Bash, and without disallowedTools also wrote. No workspace trust was given.
- Codex, evaluator subagent (2026-11-05, version 0.166.0): codex exec in a project a person had trusted listed the generated evaluator under the spawn_agent roles it sent to the model, and named and left out a malformed definition beside it.
- OpenCode, evaluator subagent (2026-11-06, version 1.19.5): opencode run listed the generated evaluator in the task tool description, while twins with no front-matter or malformed YAML were still listed with a fallback description, primary-mode and .txt twins were left out, and an invalid mode or permission stopped OpenCode at start, naming the file. No subagent was run, so read-only stays instructed.
- Claude Code, remote MCP servers (2026-11-04, version 2.1.318): from a project .mcp.json, Claude Code sent the Authorization header a ${NAME} reference named while a $NAME control went out literally; it ran a headersHelper given with --mcp-config, but refused to run one from the project file until a person trusts the workspace, and a misspelled headerHelper sent nothing.
- Codex, remote MCP servers (2026-11-04, version 0.166.0): from a project .codex/config.toml in a directory Codex had not been told to trust, codex exec sent the bearer_token_env_var and env_http_headers values and the http_headers_helper output, named a misspelled http_header_helper as ignored, and sent a ${NAME} written in http_headers literally.
- OpenCode, remote MCP servers (2026-11-04, version 1.19.5): opencode mcp list sent headers expanded from {env:NAME} in a project opencode.jsonc while a ${NAME} control went out literally; its remote server schema has no headers helper, so a server that declares one is not written for it.
- Claude Code, MCP tool restrictions (2026-11-05, version 2.1.318): claude -p with generated settings and a loopback synthetic model left the listed read tool denied by native permissions without a grant; with a grant it called only that tool, including with large arguments, and denied write, dispatcher and new tools despite readOnlyHint annotations. Unrestricted server tools ran even with a missing guard; restricted calls were held, an oversized envelope was refused, and a broken hook file was named. Project hooks still require workspace trust. Claude Code rewrites a dot in a tool name to an underscore before the hook sees it and keeps only the first of two tools that collide, so read.record and read_record are one name here.
- Codex, MCP tool restrictions (2026-11-05, version 0.166.0): codex exec with generated project enabled_tools and a loopback synthetic model called the listed read tool and rejected forced write, dispatcher and new tool calls as unsupported. The unrestricted control called all four; an empty list made no server call; a string-valued enabled_tools twin was named and rejected before startup. enabled_tools matches the server's raw tool name, so read.record and read_record stay distinct. No hook trust was granted.
- Claude Code, worktree grants (2026-11-06, version 2.1.319): in a trusted workspace the committed and .claude/settings.local.json permissions.additionalDirectories lists combined: both directories were written and an ungranted control refused; untrusted, only the local list applied, which is the one cockpit use writes, and a string-valued list in either file granted nothing from that file, without any report, while the other file's list held.
- Codex, worktree grants (2026-11-04, version 0.166.0): Codex reads no machine-local project file; --add-dir at start made the worktree writable and without it the write was refused, so cockpit use prints that flag and writes nothing.
- OpenCode, worktree grants (2026-11-04, version 1.19.5): the machine-local grant file holding the worktree path allowed the write and the control was denied, and a pattern naming a missing grant file stopped OpenCode at start, naming the file.

## Without a measurement

- Guard firing in Cursor and Grok Build: no guard adapter is checked in, so cockpit generates no guard hook.
- Instruction loading in Cursor: cockpit's instructions and the sibling guides it copies reach Cursor only through the root AGENTS.md, and .cursor/rules holds only rules overlays; no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it loads either.
- Instruction loading in Grok Build: cockpit writes the files, but no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it loads them.
- Skills in Cursor (`.cursor/skills`) and Grok Build (`.grok/skills`): cockpit writes the files, but no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it loads them.
- Session-start check in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit generates no hook for this tool.
- Evaluator subagent in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit writes the evaluator definition, but no run of the tool beside a broken control has shown that it offers it to the working agent.
- Remote MCP servers in Cursor and Grok Build: cockpit writes no remote MCP server for this tool: its remote transport and header spelling have not been checked.
- MCP tool restrictions in OpenCode, Cursor and Grok Build: no MCP tool restriction transport is implemented; restricted servers are omitted.
- Worktree grants in Cursor and Grok Build: the tool was not installed where this was measured, so cockpit use writes nothing for it.
- Browser native transports (the playwright MCP tools and the pinned Playwright CLI) in Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode: cockpit declares them and the browser skill says each still needs a person's paired call beside a broken control; no cockpit command runs or records that call, so the browser commands drive the browser through cockpit's own project client instead.
